findings.title: Date override match skips busy-time checks
findings.body: When checkIfIsAvailable finds a same-day date override that overlaps the slot, it sets dateOverrideExist and returns true immediately. That return happens before the busy.every() calendar/booking conflict check. The function is used for every fixed host (all users on personal and collective events, and fixed hosts on round-robin) and for loose round-robin hosts. On any day a host has a covering date override, existing bookings and calendar busy times are ignored, so the slot stays bookable and the host can be double-booked.

findings.title: Working-hours recheck rejects any split schedule
findings.body: The new working-hours gate uses Array.find and treats a window as a hit when the slot is outside that window. A host with two windows on the same weekday (for example 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00) therefore fails the check for every slot, because the slot is always outside at least one window, and checkIfIsAvailable returns false. end is assigned the same minutes as start, so the event length is never compared to workingHour.endTime either. This runs for every isFixed user, which includes ordinary personal events, so split-shift availability disappears from the booking page. The inverse is also wrong: if no window lists that weekday, find returns undefined and the slot is not rejected, so a fixed host with no hours that day is still treated as free.

findings.title: Override containment check is wrong for blocks and multiple ranges
findings.body: The all-day block branch compares two dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality and never succeeds, so a zero-length override (start equal to end) is not treated as blocking the day. A slot that overlaps that instant falls through and is marked available. Separately, dateOverrides.find returns true as soon as any same-day range does not cover the slot, so a second range that does cover it is ignored and the slot is rejected. A slot is also treated as inside a range on any overlap: slot start is not required to be at or after the override start, and slot end is not required to be at or before the override end, so a meeting that only partly fits the override is still offered.

findings.title: Override day match formats local time against UTC
findings.body: The same-day test compares dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format('YYYY MM DD') with slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD'). slotStartTime was created with .utc(), so its format is UTC, but the override side is a local-mode dayjs and formats in the process timezone. On any host whose local timezone is not UTC, the calendar day can differ around midnight, the override is not recognized, and the fixed-host date-override filter either does not apply or applies on the wrong day.

findings.title: Timezone-adjusted overrides lose the day and can invert
findings.body: Override start/end are shifted by inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset and then reduced with .hour() and .minute(), which wrap to 0–23 and drop any day the shift crossed. A UTC 22:00–23:30 override viewed in Asia/Kolkata becomes 03:30–05:00 on the invitee's current day instead of the next day. A short early override viewed behind UTC can wrap the end to 00:00 while the start stays late, so startTime >= endTime. buildSlots then skips that range (start >= end), but the code has already removed that user's normal working hours for the day, so the override day shows the wrong slots or none. This is the common case the timezone fix is meant to handle.

findings.title: Override minutes are shifted again by today's DST delta
findings.body: The new override math already converts wall-clock times using utcOffset at override.start for both the organizer zone and the invitee zone, so the resulting minutes are invitee-local on that date. Those minutes are then passed through buildSlots, whose getTime adds organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff (today's offset minus the target day's offset). That correction exists for weekly hours, which were shifted with today's offset, not for these overrides. When either timezone is in a different DST period today than on the booked day, every override slot moves by that extra delta, typically 60 minutes, so the bookable times do not match the saved override.

findings.title: New tests miss fixed-host overrides and real timezone shifts
findings.body: The only new assertion re-queries the same personal-event date override in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC instants as Asia/Kolkata. That does not cover the PR's main fix (round-robin slot must be hidden when a fixed host's date override makes them unavailable, including when the round-robin host is free). A +30 minute shift also never crosses midnight or a DST boundary, so the hour-wrap and DST bugs in getSlots, and the busy-time skip in checkIfIsAvailable, are not exercised.
